new_statements.rule_in_words: Gungbe is described as a tone language (two underlying tones H and L across Eastern Gbe per Gbeto 2004, whose comparison tables include Gun forms); no open source states where word stress falls or says explicitly that stress is absent or non-contrastive. The only 'stress' in the Gbe phonological literature we could see is Capo 1991 p. 22 on English loanwords whose stressed final syllable receives a falling tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: not mentioned in any opened source
new_statements.domain_note: The tonal statement is a one-line footnote in a syntax paper by a native-speaker linguist, on the Porto-Novo variety; it is not from a phonology section. The phonological descriptions of record (Hazoumé 1979, Feyer 1955, Westermann 1952, Capo 1991) were not opened.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted footnote concerns the Porto-Novo (Benin) variety of Gungbe, i.e. gunn1250 proper. Gbeto 2004 describes Wemɛgbe (Ouémé; Glottolog places Weme under Fon, fonn1241) and only uses Gun-gbe forms as comparanda. Soremekun 1987 concerns Aladagbe (Alada of Nigeria), which Glottolog tags to Gun. Nigerian sources call the language Egun/Ogu/Egungbe.
